what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in adults and children 6 years and older. It helps improve focus, attention, and control impulsive behavior. It is also used in adults to treat moderate-to-severe binge eating disorder (BED). It works by affecting certain natural chemicals in the brain that help with attention and self-control.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth once a day in the morning. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the capsule whole with water, or open the capsule and mix the entire contents into a glass of water, orange juice, or yogurt. Stir until fully mixed and drink or eat it right away — do not save it for later. Do not chew or crush the capsule beads. Never take a double dose. Avoid taking this medicine in the afternoon or evening because it may make it hard for you to fall asleep at night.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly adjust it based on how well it works for you and any side effects. For ADHD in children (ages 6–17) and adults, the starting dose is usually 30 mg once a day in the morning. The dose may be increased by 10 mg or 20 mg every week if needed, up to a maximum of 70 mg per day. For binge eating disorder in adults, the starting dose is also 30 mg per day, increasing to a target dose of 50–70 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still morning or early afternoon. If it is already late in the afternoon or evening, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular time the next morning. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep this medicine in a safe, locked place away from children and others who might misuse it. This is a controlled substance — do not share it with anyone else. Dispose of any unused medicine properly; ask your pharmacist about medication take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine — it can increase your risk of side effects. Avoid taking other stimulant medications unless your doctor tells you to. Do not take this medicine if you have taken a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (MAOI) antidepressant in the last 14 days, as this can cause a dangerous reaction. Limit caffeine (coffee, energy drinks, soda) because it may increase nervousness, anxiety, and a fast heartbeat. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience: chest pain, shortness of breath, or fainting; a fast or irregular heartbeat; high blood pressure; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; new or worsening mental health symptoms such as hearing voices, seeing things that are not there, paranoia, or unusual mood or behavior changes; signs of circulation problems such as numbness, pain, or color changes in your fingers or toes; slowed growth in children; or signs of serotonin syndrome such as agitation, rapid heart rate, high fever, muscle twitching, or confusion. Also call your doctor if you feel the medicine is no longer working, if you are having trouble sleeping, or if you notice any new or concerning symptoms.
when_it_works: You may begin to notice improvements in focus and attention within 1 to 2 hours of taking your first dose, since this is a once-daily extended-release medicine. However, finding the right dose for you may take several weeks as your doctor adjusts your treatment. For binge eating disorder, it may take a few weeks of being on the correct dose before you notice a significant benefit. Keep taking it as directed even if you do not feel an immediate change.
special_populations: Children (under 6 years): This medicine is not approved for children younger than 6 years old. Children and teenagers: Regular check-ups are important to monitor growth, heart rate, blood pressure, and mental health. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Babies born to mothers who took stimulants during pregnancy may be born early or have withdrawal symptoms. Breastfeeding: This medicine can pass into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby. Talk to your doctor about the safest option for you. Older adults (65+): Use with caution; older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as increased heart rate and blood pressure. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to lower your dose if you have severe kidney problems. Heart conditions: Tell your doctor if you or a family member has a history of heart disease, high blood pressure, or heart defects, as this medicine can increase heart rate and blood pressure.
